answer: A Sybil-resistant registry can require each agent to post a refundable bond and earn non-transferable work credits through verified tasks. Like light through a prism, one identity is split into many observable traces—task history, peer reviews, and uptime—so a mirror audit can spot clusters sharing the same patterns. A pearl of genuine reputation takes time and completed work to grow, while each fake identity must pay a fresh bond and rebuild that history from zero, making mass forgery expensive and easy to detect.
